subject: Ilvara Mizzrym
fact: Ilvara Mizzrym became a cloud of dissipating spores after the battle in Velkynvelve.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum's bolt found its target, and Grygum was likely checking on Glabbagool after the battle.
source_quote: Grygum's bolt found her. Somewhere behind me, Grygum was probably checking on Glabbagool.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir commented that the fungal destruction was 'pretty,' and caught spores during the aftermath.
source_quote: Zalthir said it was pretty. Zalthir caught some of it.

subject: Asha
fact: Asha was still praying in the dark, expecting to be answered, after the battle in Velkynvelve.
source_quote: Asha was still praying in the dark like she expected to be answered.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz was probably explaining to someone why the events of the battle were all fine.
source_quote: Daz was probably explaining to someone why exactly this was all fine.

subject: the fungus
fact: The fungus, named Dawnbringer, was destroyed in one radiant strike — a pulsating horror that took the DM weeks to stat out and folded before anyone else could act.
source_quote: The fungus, at least, was mine. Clean and total. Dawnbringer lit the thing up from the first swing and it never got a second chance — big pulsating horror that must have taken the DM weeks to stat out, and it folded before anyone else could touch it.

subject: the spores
fact: The spores were a lethal environmental hazard that punished proximity, affecting multiple characters including the narrator and Zalthir.
source_quote: Spores everywhere — the kind of death that punishes you for being nearby. I caught some of it. Zalthir caught some of it.

subject: the T'sarrans
fact: The T'sarrans were already gone from the battlefield, having withdrawn or fled after the conflict.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer, the glowing sword, pulsed once with steady warmth against the wielder's palm after the battle.
source_quote: Dawnbringer pulsed once, steady warmth against my palm.

subject: Velkynvelve
fact: Velkynvelve was the cavern battlefield where the bridge collapsed, the fungus was destroyed, and spores spread — a sprawling, chaotic environment where the narrator lost situational awareness.
source_quote: The map spread out across half the cavern and the fight kept happening somewhere I wasn't.

subject: bridge collapse
fact: The bridge in Velkynvelve collapsed, a result of prolonged effort rather than strategy, allowing passage into the cavern below.
source_quote: The bridge going down was my idea, technically, but I can't take full credit for it feeling satisfying. You swing at a bridge long enough, the bridge falls.

subject: cost of victory
fact: The true cost of winning the battle in Velkynvelve, and what it may have opened ahead, remains unknown — the Underdark has a way of correcting optimism before the equation is finished.
source_quote: I couldn't tell you yet what winning this one cost, or what it opened up ahead of us — that kind of math takes time, and the Underdark has a way of correcting your optimism before you even finish the equation.

subject: Asha's prayer
fact: Asha's continued prayer in the dark raises the unresolved question of whether she will be answered — a thread of divine hope in a world of brutal pragmatism.
source_quote: Asha was still praying in the dark like she expected to be answered. Maybe she would be. I've seen stranger things answered.

subject: the narrator
fact: The narrator, a dwarf with a glowing sword, abandoned pretense of controlling the battlefield and chose to run — accepting chaos as the only honest accounting of the battle.
source_quote: I'm a dwarf with a glowing sword in a sprawling cavern fight and at some point you stop pretending you've got angles on all of it and just pick a direction and go.

subject: aftermath
fact: The events described occurred immediately after the battle — a quiet moment of reflection as the dust settled and the consequences remained uncalculated.
source_quote: I stood there and let the quiet be quiet. We'd won.
